title: Product Grid: mobile card hierarchy, sizing, quiet wishlist
description:
GOAL

On mobile (320-430px), the product-listing grid -- the grid rhythm, the card,
and the card internals -- reads as a calm, professional e-commerce listing:
balanced proportions, clear visual hierarchy (image supports, title anchors,
price second, add + wishlist quiet), even gutters, and product titles that are
mostly readable rather than every one truncated. Fully aligned to
tailwind.config.ts tokens. Target 8+/10 on mobile card layout / hierarchy /
sizing, human live-check on :3000.

Standalone. Depends on `sang-logium-6cm` -- [Product Cards] Shared design
tokens (the brand/title/price/add type scale must be set first). Coordinates
with `sang-logium-dbu` -- [Filters] Product grid sizing fits device space,
which owns ProductCard.tsx desktop / row composition: THIS issue changes only
the mobile (< sm / 640px) rendering plus WishlistButton.tsx, and lands AFTER
dbu if dbu is mid-flight, to avoid diff conflicts.

WHAT'S WRONG NOW (observed at 320px on /products/headphones, 2-up grid)

- WishlistButton (`h-10 w-10` rounded-full, `border-border-primary` +
  `bg-surface-elevated` fill, Heart `h-5 w-5`, `right-3 top-3`, z-20): a loud
  ~40px high-contrast chip on a ~130px card. It competes with the product
  image and rivals the gold Add button. A listing-card favourite must be a
  quiet tertiary mark tucked into the corner. (design-system.md:91 already
  flags this `rounded-full` badge as off-system.)
- Every product title truncates at 2 lines ("HarmonicDyne x Z Reviews Er...",
  "Sennheiser HD 560S Open-..."). Causes: (a) the brand is shown as an eyebrow
  AND repeated at the start of the title, (b) title size vs the ~106px content
  width, (c) the 24px `gap-6` gutter stealing width from a 132px card.
- `min-h-[2.5em]` on the title (ProductCard.tsx:49) is an arbitrary bracket
  value -- off the design system.
- Grid gutter `gap-6` (24px, from gridLayout.ts `productGridClass`) is ~18% of
  a 132px card -- disproportionate for mobile; one fixed gutter is applied at
  every width.
- Hierarchy is dissonant: the bright `bg-surface-productImage` block, the loud
  wishlist chip, and the gold `btn-product-add` all shout, while the brand and
  title -- the actual identifying content -- are the weakest elements.
- Card padding: `card-product-dark` (24px) is overridden with `!p-0` then
  re-applied ad-hoc as `p-3` / `px-3 pb-3` -- no single internal rhythm.

DESIGN

- Wishlist: on the listing card, drop the filled background + border; render
  the heart as a plain icon (no chrome, or at most a subtle scrim for
  contrast), smaller visual mark, tighter into the true top-right corner.
  Keep a >= 44px hit area via padding while the visible mark stays small
  (small-visual / large-invisible-hit-slop). Keep aria-label / title / the
  signed-out redirect unchanged. NOTE: WishlistButton hardcodes its chrome in
  a raw template string (no cn / tailwind-merge), so a plain `className`
  override will not reliably win -- add a `variant` (or `size`) prop, default
  = today's PDP appearance, and select the quiet variant from ProductCard.
  ProductInfo.tsx (PDP, the only other call site) must render identically to
  now.
- Title: keep `line-clamp-2` as a safety net, but strip a leading brand token
  from the VISIBLE title when it exactly (case-insensitive) matches
  `product.brand.name` and the brand eyebrow is shown; full name stays in the
  image `alt` and the link `aria-label`. Replace `min-h-[2.5em]` with the
  spacing token equal to two title lines at the 6cm line-height; flag if no
  token fits.
- Grid gutter: make the mobile gutter proportional to the card -- a smaller
  spacing-scale step at base, restored to `gap-6` at `sm:` (mobile-first
  additive, matching gridLayout.ts's own base-then-`sm:` pattern). One edit in
  gridLayout.ts; applies to every product grid (category, all-products,
  search, wishlist).
- Internal padding: one consistent spacing-scale value on all sides of the
  content / price block; keep the image flush (`!p-0` + edge-to-edge figure)
  as dbu established.
- Hierarchy: title is the anchor (readable, not undersized), price second,
  Add tertiary-but-tappable, wishlist quietest -- achieved through the 6cm
  token sizes + the wishlist de-emphasis. Do NOT restyle the image block.
- Any h- / min-h- / max-h- / aspect- change gets the CLAUDE.md mandatory
  height-sizing diff review.

OUT OF SCOPE

- Token VALUES in tailwind.config.ts (`sang-logium-6cm`) -- flag a missing
  step, do not add one here.
- ProductCard.tsx desktop / >= sm composition, the two grid skeletons, the
  `label` prop (`sang-logium-dbu`).
- The grid COLUMN mechanism (`grid-cols-2 sm:grid-cols-products`,
  `gridTemplateColumns.products`) -- done, leave it.
- Image aspect ratio, `bg-surface-productImage` colour, `mix-blend-multiply`.
- BasketControls.tsx internals, the filter / sort surface, data / GROQ.
- Homepage card variants -- IemCard / AccessoryCard (`sang-logium-5g4.1`),
  DacCard / Featured (`sang-logium-69m`).

ACCEPTANCE -- human live-check on :3000 at 320 / 375 / 430, plus 1024+ for
no-regression, on /products/headphones AND one search results page:

1. The wishlist heart is a small quiet mark in the top-right corner -- no
   filled chip, does not compete with the image or the Add button -- and its
   tap area is still >= 44px; tapping it does not navigate to the PDP. The PDP
   wishlist button is unchanged.
2. Most product titles are readable without truncation; a long title clamps to
   2 lines with ellipsis; the brand is not repeated between the eyebrow and
   the visible title.
3. In a 2-up row with mixed title lengths, every card is the same height,
   price and Add sit on a shared baseline at the card bottom, and internal
   padding looks even on all sides.
4. The gutter between mobile cards looks proportional (not a wide channel);
   no horizontal scroll at any width; the >= sm grid and card are visually
   unchanged from before.

- Diff is tailwind.config.ts tokens only (or an explicit flag for a missing
  token). No new arbitrary bracket values.

CURRENT STATUS: Not started. Depends on `sang-logium-6cm` (token scale);
coordinate with in-progress `sang-logium-dbu` (shares ProductCard.tsx --
mobile-only edits here, land after dbu).
notes:
RISK ASSESSMENT (added 2026-08-31)

EXECUTOR: Claude Sonnet, high effort. Rationale: three files, a shared layout
primitive (gridLayout.ts feeds 4+ grids), the "WishlistButton must not change
on the PDP" constraint (needs a prop, not a className override, because the
button has no cn/tailwind-merge), the min-h token math, and the CLAUDE.md
height-sizing review gate. Not a cheap-model job.

== A. OUTCOME RISKS ==
A1. Collision with in-progress dbu on ProductCard.tsx. MITIGATE: mobile-only
    classNames (base value, restore at `sm:`); touch no `sm:`+ class dbu owns;
    land after dbu.
A2. WishlistButton change leaks to the PDP (ProductInfo.tsx) or anywhere else.
    MITIGATE: only 2 call sites -- ProductCard (listing) and ProductInfo (PDP).
    Add a `variant`/`size` prop; DEFAULT keeps today's exact classes so the PDP
    renders identically; ProductCard opts into the quiet variant. Do not
    rewrite the button's base string.
A3. Off-design-system values -- arbitrary gap / padding / size / min-h instead
    of spacing / fontSize tokens. MITIGATE: read tailwind.config.ts; tokens
    only; `min-h-[2.5em]` is itself the bug -- replace with a token, do not add
    more brackets. Flag a missing step to 6cm.
A4. gridLayout.ts gutter edit regresses desktop or the other grids (search,
    wishlist, all-products). MITIGATE: base value + `sm:gap-6` restore; human
    checks a search page too, not just category.
A5. `xs:` cascade trap -- `xs` (475px) is emitted AFTER `sm/md/lg` in this
    repo, so an `xs:` class wins at every desktop width (gridLayout.ts
    comment). MITIGATE: never use `xs:` for a value that must also hold at
    desktop; base + `sm:` only.
A6. Height-sizing ownership bug on the title min-h or any figure height.
    MITIGATE: run the CLAUDE.md mandatory height-sizing diff review on every
    h- / min-h- / max-h- / aspect- change.
A7. Scope creep into the image block, the column mechanism, dbu's composition,
    or 6cm's token values. MITIGATE: restate OUT OF SCOPE before starting; stop
    and flag if a fix needs any of them.
A8. Brand-token stripping mangles a title that legitimately starts with a word
    resembling the brand. MITIGATE: strip only an exact case-insensitive match
    of `product.brand.name` as the leading token, only when the eyebrow is
    shown; full name stays in alt / aria.
A9. False "verified" -- "quiet", "balanced", "readable hierarchy" are the
    human's call on :3000. MITIGATE: state what changed and which token drove
    it; hand the 8+/10 verdict to the human.

== B. EXECUTION RISKS ==
Lean path = edit ProductCard.tsx + WishlistButton.tsx (add a variant prop) +
gridLayout.ts only, hand off to the human on :3000.
B1. No build / tsc / ts-check / lint.
B2. No test runs, no writing tests.
B3. No agent-run dev server, no browser automation / device emulation.
B4. No npm install / new dependency.
B5. No git -- no branch, commit, push.
B6. No subagents; read the three files + tailwind.config.ts + gridLayout.ts +
    ProductInfo.tsx inline. No new docs.
B7. Minimal diff -- no reformatting untouched lines; do not "tidy" dbu's or
    6cm's in-flight changes.

Expected footprint: className edits in
app/components/features/products/ProductCard.tsx and
app/components/features/products/gridLayout.ts; a `variant`/`size` prop added
to app/components/features/wishlist/WishlistButton.tsx (default unchanged). No
new files. No deps / config / tooling changes. Any token gap is flagged to
`sang-logium-6cm`, not filled here.

title: [Cards] Brand eyebrow above title, out of image area
description:
GOAL

On every homepage IEM card and Accessory card, at every breakpoint, the brand
name renders once as an eyebrow/overline directly above the product title
(Amazon style) -- never inside or overlapping the product image.

Child of `sang-logium-5g4` -- EPIC Card Harmony. Blocks

(mechanical relocation lands first, then .1 tunes the rest). Owns the brand
line only, in IemCard.tsx and AccessoryCard.tsx.

WHAT'S WRONG NOW
- Brand is rendered twice per card: an absolutely-positioned span inside the
  image area (hidden md:block) and a second span below the image (md:hidden).
- On mobile the brand overlaps the product image / the promo badge (see
  screenshots: "64 AUDIO" behind "NEW ARRIVAL", "SVS" / "AUDIOQUEST" over the
  cable photos).

DESIGN
- Delete both existing brand spans.
- Render one brand line directly above the <h3> product title, using

- The image area contains only the image and the promo badge (NEW ARRIVAL /
  etc.) -- no text.
- IemCard keeps its brandName-derivation fallback (brand?.name, else first
  words of the product name); AccessoryCard renders the line only when
  item.brand?.name exists.
- The two files render the brand block identically.

OUT OF SCOPE
- Title weight / clamp / card height / button size -- all sang-logium-5g4.1.
- The promo badge position/style; the image ratio; padding.
- DacCard, ProductCard, data/query changes.
- Editing any tailwind.config.ts token.

ACCEPTANCE -- human live-check on :3000 at 375 / 768 / 1024-short / 1440
(max 4 tests):
1. Every card shows the brand exactly once, on its own line directly above the
   product title, at all four widths.
2. No text sits inside or over the product image -- only the promo badge.
3. The brand line is the type-product-brand eyebrow style (small, uppercase,
   letter-spaced, caption color), not bold.
4. IemCard and AccessoryCard render the brand block identically; no horizontal

WHAT'S WRONG NOW
- accessoriesBreakpointMap values may not give a balanced slides-per-view at
  each width; last row / partial peek can look awkward.
- Slide gutters (px-2 md:px-3, the -mx-3 track offset) and the gap between the

- Dots/arrows row spacing (pt-3, h-9 w-9 controls) harmony with the cards.

title: [Filters] Controls never block on pending / fetch state
description:
GOAL
The filter and sort controls stay 100% interactive at all times. A shopper can
click filters and change sort as fast and as often as they like; every click
does exactly one thing -- update the URL -- and NEVER waits on, disables, dims
to unclickable, or `pointer-events-none`s itself because a fetch, navigation or
React transition is in flight.

Layer-2 SRP fix for `sang-logium-agq` -- EPIC Filters Sorting. See also
`sang-logium-d7v` -- [Filters] Grid consumes filter+sort URL as GROQ: the
grid's refetch must never reach back and gate the controls.

THE BUG (reproduced by the owner on :3000, 2026-08-30, after S1 landed)
app/components/features/filters/FilterSidebar.tsx line ~221:
    isPending && "opacity-60 pointer-events-none"
with `isPending = useFilterSortPending()`. Before S1 the URL write was
`shallow: true`, so that transition settled within a frame and the lock was
invisible. S1 set `shallow: false` (correct -- the grid must refetch), which
stretches `isPending` across the ENTIRE Sanity round-trip. Result: clicking any
filter freezes the whole desktop sidebar until the server responds. Rapid
interaction is impossible.

ROOT CAUSE -- SRP violation
The control surface has a dependency on a downstream signal
(`useFilterSortPending`). Per the epic a control may only (a) write the URL and
(b) reflect the URL. It must not know or care whether a URL write, navigation,
transition or product fetch is settling.

SINGLE RESPONSIBILITY
Sever every coupling between the filter/sort control surface and any pending /
loading / in-flight / result-count state. Controls become always-on.

Owns:
- FilterSidebar.tsx -- remove the `isPending && "opacity-60 pointer-events-
  none"` styling and the `useFilterSortPending()` call. The sidebar wrapper is
  visually static and always interactive.
- SortBar.tsx -- remove the `isPending && ' (Loading...)'` cue and the
  `useFilterSortPending()` call. The count text stays; it is passive page data.
- useFilterSort.tsx -- URL writes KEEP running inside a React transition (so
  `loading.tsx` does not fire and the old grid stays visible), but drop the
  shared `FilterSortPendingProvider` / `useFilterSortPending` / pending context
  now that nothing in the filter layer consumes it. `useFilterParam` /
  `useClearAllFilters` fall back to plain `React.startTransition` (already the
  default-context behaviour).
- app/(store)/layout.tsx -- remove the now-unused `<FilterSortPendingProvider>`
  wrapper around {children}.
- Grep `useFilterSortPending` / `FilterSortPending` repo-wide; zero references
  in the filter layer when done.

Does NOT own: adding a pending / "updating results" affordance to the product
grid (separate, grid-owned, not requested here); the grid's GROQ translation
(S1-S4); the price slider's own internal write-debounce (F3 -- that throttles
URL writes, it is not an interactivity block, and the handle must stay live).

- When I click a filter checkbox 10 times as fast as I can, then every click
  registers immediately, the checkbox toggles on each click, and the sidebar

- When I hold-drag the price slider continuously, then the handle tracks my

- When I change sort right after clicking a filter, then the sort control
  responds instantly -- no wait for the previous fetch.
- When the network is throttled (slow 3G) and I click a filter, then the
  sidebar stays fully interactive and clickable for the entire time the grid
  is fetching; only the grid area shows work (or simply swaps when ready).
- When I rapid-toggle, then the final URL and the final grid match the final

sidebar or sort bar.

title: [Streaming] data-shown hydration mismatch on real product grid
description: Goal: /products/headphones throws a React hydration error - "A tree hydrated but some attributes of the server rendered HTML didn't match the client properties" - pointing at a next/image node (onLoad/onError) with a `data-shown=""` attribute present on the server-rendered HTML that the client tree lacks. The ported image-reveal mechanism (app/components/features/products/ImageRevealScript.tsx + reveal.module.css + ProductImage.tsx `data-reveal`) must drive the blur->sharp reveal on the real product grid WITHOUT producing any hydration mismatch. The inline REVEAL_SCRIPT's capture-phase `load` listener + MutationObserver sets `data-shown` on grid s before their Suspense chunk hydrates, so React's hydration attribute-compare flags the extra attribute - the "React never renders data-shown, so nothing reconciles it" assumption from the POC does not hold once the image lives inside a streamed boundary that hydrates later. Related: sang-logium-p0g - [Streaming] Port image-reveal mechanism to real product grid; sang-logium-7j8 - [Streaming] Product images pop in instead of revealing; sang-logium-7ao - [Streaming] Calm deliberate product image arrival; sang-logium-2de - [Product Images] Harden pipeline. A prior Haiku agent attempt closed as a false positive - the reveal mechanism was ported into app/components/features/products/ but the hydration error above is still thrown on /products/headphones, so the port is not actually working.
notes:
FIX DETERMINATION (2026-08-30) == Root cause == The reveal MUST bypass hydration - a React-gated trigger (onLoad / ref img.complete) only goes live after hydration (~15s on dev), by which point every image is complete, so all reveals flip in one post-hydration commit = one wall. That is settled (failed-attempts.md Attempts E/F.1/G/H/I). So the inline ImageRevealScript's capture-phase `load` listener is correct and must stay. The hydration error is the unavoidable side effect of that script: on a fast connection, priority/cached grid images fire `load` and get `data-shown=""` set BEFORE their Suspense chunk hydrates. When React 19 then hydrates that chunk it runs diffHydratedProperties over the (a next/image client leaf - it has onLoad/onError), finds an attribute it did not render, and throws the recoverable hydration mismatch ("...won't be patched up", diff line `- data-shown=""`). The failed-attempts.md claim - "attribute not class, React never reconciles an attribute it didn't render, so no warning" (F.3 fix, carried into Attempt I) - is WRONG for React 19. React 19 DOES flag extra server attributes on hydration. The POC only looked clean because Attempt I was verified under 3G throttling: there the image `load` events land AFTER the ~15s dev hydration, so the script sets data-shown post-hydration and React never sees it. Unthrottled on a real catalogue route the images win the race. Same latent bug lives in app/(test)/streaming-poc/page.tsx. == The proper fix == Tell React that this one element is legitimately mutated outside React, with the primitive built for exactly this ("browser extensions ... modify the HTML", timestamps, etc. - React docs): suppressHydrationWarning on the that the script targets. - app/components/features/products/ProductImage.tsx - add `suppressHydrationWarning` to the that already carries `data-reveal=""`. - app/(test)/streaming-poc/page.tsx - same one-prop add, for parity + to close the latent POC bug. (Better: both pages should share one reveal wrapper + the one ImageRevealScript - see sang-logium-p0g - so this cannot drift again.) Verified this actually reaches the : next/image spreads unknown props through to the real . get-img-props.js L130/L528 `{ ...rest }` and image-component.js L136/L171 `{ ...rest }` both pass through anything not in their known-prop lists - that is the same path `data-reveal=""` already rides. So `suppressHydrationWarning` lands on the fiber and React honours it there. Why this is the right call, not a patch-over: - suppressHydrationWarning is one element deep, attributes/text only. The is a leaf. It does NOT disable hydration, does NOT make anything a client component, does NOT touch the Suspense streaming. Zero blast radius. - The server/client render of the IS genuinely identical (React renders the same thing both sides); the only divergence is the script's out-of-band data-shown. That is precisely, semantically, what the prop is for. - Keeps the trigger off React => streaming UX (7ao / 7j8 hard constraint) and the no-wall reveal both stay intact. Diff: 1 line per page (2 lines total), no new files, no script change, no CSS change. == Fallback (only if a future next/image drops the passthrough) == Move the flip off the onto the plain wrapper
ProductImage renders directly (guaranteed to forward suppressHydrationWarning): - script: `e.target.closest('[data-reveal]')?.setAttribute('data-shown','')`, move `data-reveal=""` onto the wrapper div, keep it React-rendered. - div gets `suppressHydrationWarning`. - reveal.module.css: `.reveal[data-shown]` -> `[data-reveal][data-shown] .reveal`, `.wrap:has(img[data-shown])` -> `.wrap[data-shown]`. The is then never script-touched. Bigger diff; not needed today. == Do NOT == - Do not gate data-shown on a "hydration complete" signal / rIC / post-hydration flush - that re-batches into one wall (the whole reason for the script). - Do not reintroduce a "use client" reveal leaf per tile (F.1: 30 leaves hydrate in one pass = wall; recorded hard constraint on 7j8). - Do not add placeholder="blur" back (D: next/image then re-renders the on load and clobbers the attribute).

title: [Filters] Grid consumes filter+sort URL as GROQ
description:
GOAL
Whatever filter/sort state is present in the URL (the nuqs-based F1 contract:
?sort= ?minPrice= ?maxPrice= ?inStock= ?brand= ?page=), the product grid fetches
from Sanity exactly the set of products that URL describes -- correct on first
paint, on refresh, on Back/Forward, and from a shared link. Same URL => same
products, every time.

This is the "grid consumption" layer that the epic `sang-logium-agq` -- EPIC
Filters Sorting explicitly defers to its own issue. F1-F6 own writing the URL and
rendering the controls to match it; THIS work owns reading the URL and
translating it into the GROQ query. Single responsibility of the product grid:
read the URL, fetch the perfect match of products for that URL state.

DESIGN -- verified against Next.js 15 / React 19 / nuqs / GROQ docs + reference
implementations (evidence in NOTES):

SP1  URL searchParams are the single source of truth. The grid's Server
     Component reads `await searchParams` and is the sole consumer. No store,
     no client filter state, no second reader.

SP2  Client controls write with nuqs `shallow: false` so the Server Component
     re-runs with fresh searchParams and refetches. Per the nuqs docs this
     option exists precisely to "render the RSC tree based on the updated
     query state".

SP3  One pure translation: urlState -> { order, where, params }. Sort is a
     fixed allowlist (F1 already enforces it). Every value goes through GROQ
     `$params` -- never string-interpolated (GROQ params are injection-safe by
     design). Server-side only; no second translation anywhere.

SP4  Writes are wrapped in useTransition. While the RSC payload streams, the
     controls + grid show a pending state (dim / data-pending) and stay
     mounted and interactive. No loading.tsx / full-page skeleton on a filter
     change.

SP5  Result count, pagination and empty state derive from the SAME filtered
     query -- count reflects the narrowed set, page clamps to the new total,
     page resets to 1 on any filter change.

SP6  Sort mapping:
       featured   -> order(coalesce(displayPriority,0) desc, _createdAt desc)
       price-asc  -> order(price_data.unit_amount asc)
       price-desc -> order(price_data.unit_amount desc)
       newest     -> order(_createdAt desc)

SP7  Filter predicates (all parameterized):
       minPrice/maxPrice -> price_data.unit_amount >= $minCents && <= $maxCents
                            (URL carries whole dollars; x100 at this edge)
       inStock=true      -> stock - reservedStock > 0
       brand=a,b         -> brand->slug.current in $brands (slugs lowercased
                            both sides)

SCOPE: catalogue routes only -- /products (All Products) and
/products/[...slug] (category). Search, brand pages, saved lists: not here.

OUT OF SCOPE
- No `category` / form-factor facet. The product schema has no field for it and
  such a filter should not exist. If an F5 category checkbox group ships, it
  stays inert against the grid.

  placeholder; a separate concern.

SPLIT -- 4 children, in sequence, each independently live-checkable on :3000:
  S1  [Filters] Grid re-fetches on URL change + sort key
  S2  [Filters] Price range + in-stock -> GROQ where
  S3  [Filters] Brand facet -> GROQ where
  S4  [Filters] Filtered count, empty state, page clamp, back/fwd
S1 first (it carries the shallow:false flip + the translation skeleton that
S2/S3 fill in). S2 and S3 run in either order after S1. S4 last.

ACCEPTANCE -- whole feature, human live-check on :3000 (/products and
/products/headphones):
- When I open /products/headphones?sort=price-asc directly, then the grid is
  ordered cheapest-first from the first paint (no unsorted flash).
- When I change any filter/sort control, then the grid updates to the exact
  matching set with no full-page white reload and without the sidebar
  disappearing.
- When I apply brand + price + in-stock + sort together, then the grid shows
  only products matching ALL of them, in the chosen order, and the result
  count matches what is shown.

  every time.

  clear filters, not a broken or infinite-loading grid.

this. F1 URL contract + controls exist; the grid does not read the contract.
notes:
DESIGN EVIDENCE (checked 2026-08-30)

First principles:
- The URL query string IS the filter/sort state (shareable, bookmarkable,
  survives refresh + Back/Forward for free). Not component state, not a store.
- The product set is a pure function of the URL: products = f(urlState). Same
  URL => same products. So f is computed in exactly ONE place.
- Fetching belongs where the data, the token and the request cache live: the
  server. The browser never builds the product query.
- URL values are untrusted input: allowlist the sort key, parameterize every
  value into GROQ.

Sources:
- nuqs official docs, Options: "pair shallow:false with the searchParams page
  prop to render the RSC tree based on the updated query state"; the
  startTransition option surfaces isLoading while the server streams the RSC
  payload. https://nuqs.dev/docs/options
- Next.js docs, page.js `searchParams` prop = the App Router mechanism for
  filter / sort / pagination driven by the URL.
- Aurora Scharff, "Managing Advanced Search Param Filtering in the Next.js App
  Router" (reference implementation, developed with the nuqs maintainer): URL
  as single source of truth; client control -> shallow:false -> server
  refetch; useTransition for pending; pitfalls -- "avoid full-page loading
  skeletons, keep controls mounted and responsive", "don't use local useState
  for filter state", "consolidate filter updates into a single transition".
  https://aurorascharff.no/posts/managing-advanced-search-param-filtering-next-app-router/
- Vercel Next.js Commerce: same shape -- client control updates URLSearchParams,
  server component reads the searchParams prop and refetches sorted/filtered.
- Sanity GROQ params docs: "$"-parameters are JSON literals substituted before
  execution, "safe to pass from user input" (injection-proof).
  https://www.sanity.io/docs/groq-parameters

Accepted tradeoff: reading searchParams opts the catalogue routes into dynamic
rendering, and each filter change is a server round-trip to Sanity. This is
inherent to faceted commerce filtering and is covered by React cache() dedup +
Sanity CDN + the transition keeping the old grid visible + history:push making
Back instant.

== COORDINATION RISK ==
R1. An agent implements against this issue directly and builds all four slices
    at once. MITIGATE: this is coordination-only. Execute S1 -> (S2, S3) -> S4,
    one at a time; each has its own risk assessment and lean-path guard.
R2. The layer boundary erodes -- a slice starts reading the grid's rendered
    output or product data to "check its work". MITIGATE: every slice's only
    input is the parsed F1 state; its only output is a GROQ fragment. The live
    check is the human's on :3000.
== EXECUTOR STRATEGY (added 2026-08-30) ==

This issue: no executor -- coordination only. Do not implement against d7v.

Fan-out across the 4 children -- 2 expensive, 2 cheap, gated by the human's
:3000 live check:

  S1  sang-logium-ytc  -> Claude Sonnet (Cline)     [architecture-sensitive]
  S2  sang-logium-pkt  -> DeepSeek V4 (Cline)       [contained pure fn]
  S3  sang-logium-5gr  -> DeepSeek V4 (Cline)       [contained pure fn]
  S4  sang-logium-8or  -> Claude Sonnet (Cline)     [integration surface]

ORDER (do not parallelise across the gate):
  1. S1 on Sonnet. Human live-checks all 4 acceptance lines on :3000.
     STOP here if any fail -- S2/S3/S4 build on this foundation; cheap rework
     on a broken mechanism is the expensive failure mode.
  2. S2 + S3 on DeepSeek V4 -- ideally ONE Cline session back-to-back (both
     only edit buildProductQuery.ts, so repo context is loaded once). Human
     live-checks each.
  3. S4 on Sonnet -- needs S1+S2+S3 merged so there is a real filtered result
     set to test count / empty / clamp / back-fwd against.

WHY THIS SPLIT OF MODELS:
- Sonnet only where a wrong-but-plausible diff survives review: S1 (RSC wiring,
  shallow flip, must not collapse per-chunk streaming -- AI_LESSONS L02) and
  S4 (multi-file integration, subtle correctness: gate empty on resolved count
  not empty chunk, clamp ordering, back/forward restore).
- DeepSeek V4 (not Haiku / Flash) for S2/S3: one file, airtight spec, and the
  per-issue A-risks are sufficient guardrails -- but GROQ reference deref (->)
  and `in $array` semantics are a known hallucination trap, so not the
  cheapest tier.
- Cline is the harness for all four.

Sibling cleanup: sang-logium-kl5 — Catalogue: remove dead category facet. Land it before S2/S3 (shared file filterSortParams.ts). Category is not part of grid consumption.
== INVARIANT: THE CONTROLS ARE NEVER BLOCKED (added 2026-08-30) ==

The filter/sort controls MUST stay fully interactive at ALL times -- no matter
how rapid or frequent the clicks. NOTHING downstream of the URL write may gate
them: no `disabled`, no `pointer-events-none`, no opacity-to-unclickable, no
debounce-into-unresponsiveness, no waiting on a transition / navigation /
Sanity fetch to settle.

A control's only two jobs:
  1. write the URL synchronously via nuqs on interaction,
  2. render its own state to match the URL.
It must not read, or react to, any "URL update in flight" / "grid refetching" /
pending / loading / result-count signal. Any pending or stale-results
affordance belongs to the PRODUCT GRID, never to the control surface.

title: [Filters] Shared URL param contract for filter + sort state
description:
SINGLE RESPONSIBILITY: This issue defines the single shared vocabulary for filter/sort URL state - every param key, its value type, its default, its parse and serialize rules, the history mode (replace vs push), and the clean-URL rule (a param sitting at its default never appears in the URL) - as nuqs parsers plus a loader, exported for F2-F6 to import. It also defines the shared "pending" affordance shown while a URL transition is in flight. It is headless: no visible UI of its own. It does not fetch data and does not know about, import, query, or react to the product grid, product data, result counts, or streaming.

ACCEPTANCE TESTS - human live check on the dev server at localhost:3000. F1 has no UI, so these are checked by hand-typing catalogue URLs and watching the address bar, verified against the first consuming control (F2) once it exists:

- When I load a catalogue URL with a filter/sort param set to its default value, then once the page settles the address bar shows that param removed (defaults never persist in the URL).
- When I load a catalogue URL with a filter/sort param holding a junk value, then the page still renders (no crash, no error overlay) and the param is treated as unset.
- When I change one filter/sort control and then press the browser Back button, then the address bar returns to the exact previous URL, and Forward re-applies it.
- When I change a control, then the page does not do a full white reload - the change is a soft URL update.
- When any control writes the URL, then unrelated query params already present (e.g. ?q= from search, ?page= from pagination) are preserved untouched.

OUT OF SCOPE
- Any visible control (V1/V2 and F2-F6).
- Whether the product grid reacts to the params (page-composition concern, not this contract).
- Keyboard and screen-reader behaviour.

RISK ASSESSMENT

Outcome risks (wrong result / mix-up / hallucination / false positive)
- Reviving the deleted lib/catalogue/filterParams.ts / sortParams.ts / searchParams.ts verbatim. They encoded the OLD removed system's shape (compound ?f=brand:x syntax, a server-side sort allowlist, shallow:false + router.replace to force an RSC refetch). Mitigation: design the contract fresh for the V1/F-layer's client-only needs; treat the deleted files as reference for nuqs mechanics only, not for the schema or the routing model.
- Param-key collisions. /products and /products/[...slug] already parse ?page= by hand; /search owns ?q=. Mitigation: enumerate every param already read on those three routes first; choose filter keys that never clash; the contract must round-trip unrelated params untouched.
- Wrong history/shallow choice. The old system used shallow:false to trigger a server round-trip; this layer is client-only display sync and almost certainly wants shallow:true (no refetch) with an explicit replace-vs-push decision per param. Mitigation: state the choice and its consequence in the contract; the Product Grid observes URL changes independently via the existing lib/catalogue/urlChangeEvents.ts (locationchange) - filters never call the grid.
- Clean-URL rule wrong: defaults serialized into the URL. This makes URLs ugly and trips lib/catalogue/seo.ts isFacetedQuery (canonical/noindex logic keys off query presence). Mitigation: default value => param absent; sanity-check against isFacetedQuery.
- Price unit ambiguity. Product price_data.unit_amount is cents; the UI works in dollars (lib/catalogue/priceBounds.ts, centsToDisplay). Mitigation: the contract fixes the URL unit explicitly (dollars, integer) and F3 converts for display; write it down.
- "Does changing a filter reset ?page=?" left undecided, so F2-F6 each guess. Mitigation: decide it here (recommended: a filter/sort write resets page to 1) and expose it as one helper the controls call.
- nuqs API drift. Installed is nuqs ^2.8.3. Mitigation: confirm the exact installed version and the API surface used (parseAsString/parseAsInteger/parseAsArrayOf, useQueryState(s), createLoader/createSerializer) before writing.

Execution risks (unnecessary work / time cost)
- Headless issue => strongest pull to "just run tsc / a build to check it compiles". Mitigation: none of tsc / ts-check / build / lint / tests / npm install - inspection only.
- No dev server: F1 has no UI; verification piggybacks on F2. Mitigation: do not start a server or browser automation.
- Writing a separate contract design doc. Mitigation: the contract lives in code + this issue body; no new docs.
- Over-scoping into GROQ filter-builders, Sanity loaders, or grid wiring. Mitigation: headless parsers + a loader/serializer only; zero data access; no commit/push unless asked.

Expected footprint: one small module under lib/catalogue/ (e.g. filterSortParams.ts) exporting the parsers, a loader, a serializer and the page-reset helper. No component, dependency or config changes.

SEQUENCE: Can start immediately (independent of V1). Blocks F2-F6.

CURRENT STATUS: Not started. nuqs is already a project dependency (^2.8.3); no filter/sort param contract exists on main.

title: [Filters] Desktop filter panel + sort bar visual shell
description:
SINGLE RESPONSIBILITY: This issue delivers only the static desktop appearance of the filters/sorting surface, built from the project design system (tailwind.config.ts tokens + type-* utilities), matching the archived components at commit f4f3026a^ (app/components/features/filters/: FilterSidebar, PriceRangeSlider, SortDropdown, and the shared section-header / slider primitives they export). It does not read or write the URL, does not use query params, does not fetch data, and does not filter, sort, count, or otherwise touch the product grid or streaming. All options, counts and price bounds are hardcoded placeholders. Any state is local and cosmetic only (expand/collapse a group, ticked look).

ACCEPTANCE TESTS - human live check on the dev server at localhost:3000, desktop-width window, on a category page (e.g. /products/headphones) and on /products:

Layout
- When I open the page at desktop width, then I see a filter panel on the left and the product grid to its right.
- When I look at the filter panel, then it reads as one finished card (soft border, slightly raised background, same visual language as other cards on the site), not a plain box bolted on.

Panel contents
- When I look at the panel top, then I see a "Filters" heading.
- When I scan down the panel, then I see, in this order: a price range control, an "In stock only" checkbox, a "Brand" group, and at least one more facet group.
- When I look at the price control, then I see a two-handle slider with min and max value labels, and the track / handle / gold active-fill match the site's design system.
- When I look at the "Brand" group, then I see a group label and a list of options, each with a checkbox and a small count beside it.
- When a brand option has a count of zero, then it appears dimmed / disabled.
- When I check fonts, colours and spacing against the rest of the site, then nothing looks like a raw browser default (no blue underlined links, no system font, no misaligned native checkboxes).

Sort + count bar
- When I look above the product grid, then I see a "Sort by" control and a line showing a result count.
- When I open the sort control, then I see a list of options (Featured, Price low-to-high, Price high-to-low, Newest, Name A-Z).

Cosmetic interactions (look only)
- When I click a group header (e.g. "Brand"), then that group collapses and hides its options; clicking again expands it.
- When I click a checkbox, then it shows a ticked state.
- When I pick a different sort option, then the control's label updates to show my choice.

Nothing actually works (the hard guarantee)
- When I tick/untick any checkbox, drag the price handles, collapse a group, or change the sort option, then the product grid stays identical (same products, same order, same count).
- When I do any of the above, then the page URL stays exactly the same (no query params appear).
- When I reload the page, then every checkbox and collapsed group returns to its default look (nothing was remembered).

OUT OF SCOPE
- Narrow / mobile / tablet widths and the lg-touch breakpoint (handled in V2).
- Keyboard and screen-reader behaviour (later layer).
- Any URL, data, or product-grid behaviour (functional layer F1-F6).

RISK ASSESSMENT

Outcome risks (wrong result / mix-up / hallucination / false positive)
- Wrong source: f4f3026a is the DELETION commit; the components live at its parent f4f3026a^. Mitigation: read via `git show f4f3026a^:app/components/features/filters/<file>`.
- Porting the wired archive by mistake. Two archived copies exist: the static one at app/components/features/filters/ (f4f3026a^) and a fully URL-wired one at product-building-center/filters_archived/ (with useFilterNuqs / useRangeSlider / useDrawerState). Mitigation: copy only from the static path; never open filters_archived/; strip any import of a hook, store, useSearchParams, nuqs or router; options/counts/bounds stay hardcoded inline.
- "Finishing" the feature: adding real state, URL or data because it feels unfinished. Mitigation: the "Nothing actually works" acceptance tests are the gate - any wiring shipped fails the issue.
- Design-token drift. The archived components mix token names from different eras (text-text-accent vs text-accent-500, bg-surface-elevated, type-overline, bg-brand-100). Some resolve on current main, some may not. Mitigation: carry the archived classes over, then grep tailwind.config.ts and app/globals.css to confirm each class exists; for the card shell reuse an existing sibling card's exact border/bg/shadow classes; no raw hex, no default palette, no invented class names.
- Real data creeping in: fetching brands or counts from Sanity to look realistic. Mitigation: hardcoded arrays only; no GROQ; no imports from sanity-cms/.
- Wrong stock control: porting the archived StockMinimumSlider. Mitigation: "In stock only" is a plain checkbox using the existing app/components/ui/Checkbox.tsx - the archived slider is not used.
- Grid-column layout / height regression. The sidebar adds sticky / self-start / height classes next to ChunkedProductGrid, and CLAUDE.md has a mandatory review gate for any h-full / min-h- / max-h- / aspect- change under app/components/**. Mitigation: additive only (new sidebar column + toolbar as siblings in the products route); do not edit ChunkedProductGrid / Pagination / ShopHeader / streaming files; run the height/sizing diff review before done.
- Confusing current uncommitted streaming WIP with the archived state. The working tree already has many modified product/streaming files. Mitigation: do not touch modified files; new components go in a fresh app/components/features/filters/; read on-disk state as it is now.
- Claiming visual correctness the agent cannot see. Mitigation: the deliverable is source that compiles and matches the archived structure + verified tokens; state which sibling component was mirrored, then stop - the when/then list is the human's :3000 verdict.
- Scope bleed into V2 / F1-F6: adding responsive breakpoints, lg-touch, keyboard/ARIA, or real sort/filter logic. Mitigation: desktop width only, static only; re-read OUT OF SCOPE before starting.

Execution risks (unnecessary work / time cost)
- Running heavy commands: tsc / ts-check, npm run build / next build, project-wide eslint/prettier, test suites, npm install. Mitigation: none of these - forbidden by CLAUDE.md and the user's standing rule; TS/style correctness by inspection, matching surrounding code.
- Spinning up a dev server or browser automation to "verify". Mitigation: the human runs the :3000 live check; no preview_start, no screenshots, no Playwright.
- Adding dependencies (a slider or dropdown library). Mitigation: the archived PriceRangeSlider is hand-rolled markup - reuse it; zero new deps.
- Over-abstracting: generic facet registry, shared hooks, Storybook, unit tests for static markup. Mitigation: near-verbatim copy of the archived components + minimal mount into the two listing pages; no tests at this layer.
- Over-exploring: grepping the whole repo, restoring the deleted docs/catalogue-filters-*.md set, spawning a research subagent, or re-deriving the products route. Mitigation: the only reads needed are the named archived components at f4f3026a^, tailwind.config.ts, app/globals.css, one sibling card, and the two products page.tsx files (plus docs/homepage-structure.md for section composition).
- Writing new audit/architecture docs or long analysis. Mitigation: read, build, stop. No commit or push unless asked.

Expected footprint: ~3-5 new files under app/components/features/filters/, plus one small edit to each of app/(store)/products/page.tsx and app/(store)/products/[...slug]/page.tsx to mount the panel + sort/count bar. No dependency, config or tooling changes.

SEQUENCE: First issue. No dependencies.

title: EPIC Filters Sorting
description:
GOAL: Anywhere a shopper faces a list of products (category pages, All Products, search, brand pages, saved lists), they can narrow and reorder it the way a serious audio retailer would allow: controls that are obvious and one action away, updates that feel instant and never shift the page, a view that survives refresh / back / a shared link, and behaviour that is identical on phone and desktop.

APPROACH — strict layering:
- Layer 1 (visual): how the surface looks. Desktop first (V1), then responsive (V2). Zero behaviour.
- Layer 2 (functional): the filters/sorting component's only job is the URL. On user interaction it writes the URL via nuqs; on URL change it renders its own controls to match the URL. It never imports, queries, or reacts to the product grid, product data, result counts, or streaming. One control per issue (F1-F6).

SUPERSEDES: sang-logium-bsr (Catalogue filters G1-G18) and sang-logium-abo (Search G1-G9), both closed as obsolete - they describe the filters/sorting system removed from main in f4f3026a.

ISSUES: V1, V2, F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6. Not linked as deps/children - sequence is coordinated here and noted in each issue body.

CURRENT STATUS: Not started. main has no filter or sort UI on any product list.
notes:
RISK ASSESSMENT (added 2026-08-30)

This is an EPIC, not an execution target. No agent should implement against this issue directly.

== KEY RISKS (coordination / outcome) ==

R1. An agent picks up the epic and builds the whole surface at once, defeating the strict
    layering.
    MITIGATE: execute only the child issues, one at a time, in sequence:
    F1 and V1 can run in parallel -> then V2 (after V1) -> F2-F5 (after F1 + V1) -> F6 last.

R2. Layer boundary erodes across issues.
    A functional issue starts reading the grid / data / counts "because it's easier".
    MITIGATE: every F-issue's only inputs are props + the F1 URL contract. If a task can't be
    done within that, the boundary is wrong - stop and re-scope, do not cross it.

R3. Re-introducing the removed system.
    This epic SUPERSEDES sang-logium-bsr and sang-logium-abo; the old filters/sorting system was
    deleted in f4f3026a and must not be resurrected wholesale - only the design-system-aligned
    V1 shells are reused, markup only.

R4. Grid reactivity gets built inside a V/F issue.
    Whether the product grid actually filters / sorts / counts is page-composition, explicitly
    out of scope of every V and F issue.
    MITIGATE: keep it out; that is a later, separate concern with its own issue.

== EXECUTION NOTE ==

No execution-risk list here - nothing is built against this issue. The lean-path and
no-build/no-lint/no-dev-server/ignore-git rules live on each child issue.

== INVARIANT: THE CONTROLS ARE NEVER BLOCKED (added 2026-08-30) ==

The filter/sort controls MUST stay fully interactive at ALL times -- no matter
how rapid or frequent the clicks. NOTHING downstream of the URL write may gate
them: no `disabled`, no `pointer-events-none`, no opacity-to-unclickable, no
debounce-into-unresponsiveness, no waiting on a transition / navigation /
Sanity fetch to settle.

A control's only two jobs:
  1. write the URL synchronously via nuqs on interaction,
  2. render its own state to match the URL.
It must not read, or react to, any "URL update in flight" / "grid refetching" /
pending / loading / result-count signal. Any pending or stale-results
affordance belongs to the PRODUCT GRID, never to the control surface.

Violation found 2026-08-30: FilterSidebar applied `opacity-60 pointer-events-
none` while `useFilterSortPending()` was true; S1's `shallow: false` stretched
that "pending" window across the whole server round-trip, locking the sidebar
on every click. Fix tracked in `sang-logium-aks` -- [Filters] Controls never
block on pending / fetch state (do it before S2/S3).

title: [Product Images] Harden pipeline + replace invalid inventory images
description:
﻿Some inventory images across the product catalogue are currently forged/invalid and must be replaced in bulk. Additionally, the product image upload pipeline must be hardened so that uploaded images never include backgrounds and never exceed acceptable size limits.

The project already has a dedicated external data folder (with dashes in its name, located outside the repo root) that contains RemBG background-removal tooling and image size-management utilities. The replacement and upload pipeline should be wired to run product images through that folder's existing processing steps.

Please begin by:

- Auditing the current product image inventory and pipeline to identify all forged/invalid images and their source/Sanity mappings.
- Inspecting the external Sanglogium data folder to document the existing RemBG and image-size-management capabilities.
- Proposing a replacement pipeline that removes backgrounds, enforces size limits, validates output, and re-uploads only clean images.
- Implementing the minimal safe first slice to prevent new invalid images from entering the pipeline.

## Proposed remaining pipeline steps

### Phase 0 — Audit current inventory

1. Run a Sanity-wide audit of every `product` document, collecting for each main image and gallery image:
   - `_id`, `name`, `slug`, `catalogueLocationKeys`
   - `image.asset._ref`, `originalFilename`, `url`, `metadata.dimensions`, `sha1hash`
   - duplicate-asset counts across products
2. Flag as invalid any image that is:
   - missing or tiny (`< 200px`)
   - a placeholder/wrong filename
   - a duplicate shared by more than 2 products
   - a main product image with a non-transparent / non-removed background
   - over size limits (`> 1 MB` main, `> 1.2 MB` gallery, or `> 1600px` max dimension)
3. Output `image-audit-report.json` with severity groups and source-to-Sanity mappings.

### Phase 1 — Harden the ingestion pipeline (minimal safe first slice)

1. Add a post-processing validation step to `sang-logium-data/src/image-pipeline.ts` that runs **after** `rembg_remove.py` / `compress_gallery.py` and **before** `assets.upload`:
   - Main image: PNG must have alpha; edges must be > 70% transparent; dimensions and file size must be under `1600px` / `1 MB`.
   - Gallery image: JPEG must be under `1600px` / `1.2 MB`; quality no lower than `75`.
   - Failures are rejected and logged; no bad asset enters Sanity.
2. Wire `sang-logium` (main repo) manual image paths to the external pipeline:
   - Add a small adapter script in `sang-logium` that calls `sang-logium-data/scripts/rembg_remove.py` and `compress_gallery.py` for any image before it is uploaded/patched.
   - Update `scripts/patch-botched-product-images.mjs` to route each image through the adapter and apply the same validation.

### Phase 2 — Bulk replacement of existing invalid images

1. From the audit report, build a queue of products whose images need replacement.
2. For each product, fetch the original high-res source (re-scrape source, e-commerce page, or existing Sanity asset).
3. Run the source through the now-validated `sang-logium-data` pipeline:
   - Main image → `rembg_remove.py` → validate → upload → patch product `image`.
   - Gallery image → `compress_gallery.py` → validate → upload → patch product `gallery[]`.
4. Re-verify each product after upload (new `sha1hash`, new dimensions, not the old bad asset).
5. Track completed products and update the audit report.

### Phase 3 — Ongoing monitoring and documentation

1. Add `scripts/validate-product-images.mjs` to the main repo for periodic re-checks.
2. Integrate the validation gate into `sang-logium-data/scripts/batch-run.ts` so every future batch upload is pre-validated.
3. Document the final pipeline in `_project/reusables/product-image-pipeline.md`.

### External tooling to use

- `C:\webdev\sang-logium-data\scripts\rembg_remove.py` — RemBG background removal, resize to `1600px`, compress to `<= 1 MB` PNG.
- `C:\webdev\sang-logium-data\scripts\compress_gallery.py` — RGB JPEG compression, `1600px`, `<= 1.2 MB`, quality `90-75`.
- `C:\webdev\sang-logium-data\src\image-pipeline.ts` — existing orchestration for download → process → upload.
- `C:\webdev\sang-logium\sanity-cms\lib\backendClient.ts` / `SANITY_STUDIO_READ_WRITE` — for patching product references in the main repo.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Audit report lists every invalid product image with reason and source mapping.
- [ ] New validation gate in `sang-logium-data/src/image-pipeline.ts` rejects bad images before upload.
- [ ] Manual image patch path in `sang-logium` uses the external RemBG/compress tools and validation.
- [ ] All previously flagged main product images are replaced with background-removed, size-limited assets.
- [ ] Re-audit shows zero invalid images.
notes:
RISK ASSESSMENT (added 2026-08-30)

== A. OUTCOME RISKS (wrong result, mix-up, hallucination, quality drop) ==

A1. Scope explosion.
    The issue lists Phases 0-3. Only the "minimal safe first slice" (Phase 1: the post-processing
    validation gate) is wanted now.
    MITIGATE: implement the validation step + reject/log, then STOP. Phases 2-3 (bulk re-scrape,
    ongoing monitoring) are separate slices - flag them, don't do them.

A2. Destructive Sanity writes.
    Bulk patching product image references in the live CMS is irreversible and high blast radius.
    MITIGATE: no bulk upload / patch in this slice. Any write path is dry-run first and
    human-confirmed per batch.

A3. Hallucinating "forged/invalid" images.
    Deciding an image is fake on vibes.
    MITIGATE: use ONLY the issue's explicit flags - missing/tiny (<200px), placeholder/wrong
    filename, duplicate shared by >2 products, non-transparent main-image background, over size
    limits (>1MB main / >1.2MB gallery / >1600px). Output a report; do not act on judgement calls.

    Editing C:\webdev\sang-logium-data (external repo) carelessly.

A5. Environment assumptions.

    MITIGATE: verify the tooling exists before wiring to it; do not run heavy batch jobs.

A6. Sandbox cannot reach Sanity.
    api.sanity.io is blocked by allowlist in this environment; a full Sanity-wide audit crawl
    will not run here.
    MITIGATE: write the audit query/script and hand the actual run to the human (or the browser
    GET path). Don't burn retries on blocked curl.

== B. EXECUTION RISKS (agent adds fat instead of the lean path) ==

Lean path = write the validation gate + the audit script, propose Phases 2-3. No bulk runs.

B1. No npm install / pip install unprompted.
B2. No full catalogue crawl or source re-scrape in this environment.
B3. No bulk Sanity writes - the human runs those, per batch, after review.
B4. No build / lint / test of either repo.

B7. Ignore git in both repos - no commits.

Expected footprint: a validation function in sang-logium-data/src/image-pipeline.ts + one audit
script in sang-logium; a short written proposal for Phases 2-3.

title: [Filters] Price slider: hairline track + refined thumbs
notes:
GOAL (verbatim): Refined visual UX look of the price slider bar and its dots. Should be
thinner and more rarified look.

Current status: PriceRangeSlider.tsx renders a 4px (`h-1`) fully-gold rounded bar with two
12px (`h-3 w-3`) cream discs (`bg-brand-400` #F6E3D5) ringed in a 1px gold border
(`accent-500` #D4AF37). Because both handles rest at the bounds by default, the active
gold fill spans the whole track edge-to-edge -> reads as one heavy gold "dumbbell", not a
filter control. Handles are flat (no elevation) and low-contrast where they sit on the
gold fill. Functional; URL wiring, debounce, clamp, reset all correct and untouched by
this issue.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
WHAT PROFESSIONAL E-COMMERCE / DESIGN-SYSTEM SLIDERS DO (research, Sept 2026)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Consensus "thin / refined" range-slider anatomy across MUI, Radix/shadcn, Ant Design,
Material 3, Chakra:

  - Rest track thickness:   2-4px, fully rounded. (MUI rail 2px; Ant 4px; Material 4px;
                            Radix h-1.5 = 6px is the thick end.)
  - Active fill:             same thickness as rest track, accent colour, ONLY the
                            segment between the two handles.
  - Thumb visible size:      12-16px. (MUI small 12px; Ant 10-12px; Radix 16px.)
  - Thumb fill:              near-white / surface colour, NOT the accent colour. A solid
                            accent-filled disc reads heavy; a light disc with a thin
                            accent ring reads precise.
  - Thumb edge:              1px accent border (Ant) or 2px (Radix) + a soft drop shadow
                            so it lifts off the track. On a dark UI the shadow is what
                            stops it looking pasted-on.
  - Hit target:              visual thumb stays small; the *interactive* area is expanded
                            invisibly to >=24px (44px on touch) via a transparent pad.
                            Baymard: over-sensitive handles are the #1 dual-slider
                            complaint - keep the grab area generous.
  - Hover / active:          subtle - border lightens one step and/or thumb scales ~1.1.
  - Focus-visible:           2px accent outline, small offset.
  - End labels ($0 / $1000): small, muted, tight leading under the track.

Sources:
  - Baymard, "Improve Form Slider UX" - https://baymard.com/blog/slider-interfaces
  - Baymard dual-slider findings (>50% misread dual-point price sliders)
  - Setproduct, "Slider UI design" - https://www.setproduct.com/blog/slider-ui-design
  - Material 3 Sliders - https://m3.material.io/components/sliders/specs
  - MUI Slider / Radix Slider / Ant Design Slider component specs

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
TARGET SPEC FOR THIS COMPONENT (apply exactly; dark UI, existing tokens)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
File: app/components/features/filters/PriceRangeSlider.tsx  (ONLY this file)

1. Rest track
   - Height 2px: `h-1` -> `h-0.5` on the gradient div in `DualRangeSlider`.
   - Colour unchanged: `TRACK_REST` = `secondary-700` #4A4948.
   - Keep `rounded-full`, keep `inset-x-0`.
   - Re-centre it in the row: `top-1.5` -> `top-2` (row stays `h-4`), i.e. vertically
     centred on the 16px row.

2. Active fill
   - Same 2px height (it is the same gradient div - nothing to change structurally).
   - Colour unchanged: `TRACK_ACTIVE_FILL` = `accent-500` #D4AF37.
   - No behaviour change: it still spans handle-to-handle. At full range that is still
     edge-to-edge, but at 2px it now reads as a hairline, not a bar. (Do NOT add
     logic to hide it at full range - that is behaviour, out of scope.)

3. Thumbs (`THUMB_CLASSES`, both `::-webkit-slider-thumb` and `::-moz-range-thumb`)
   - Size unchanged at 12px (`h-3 w-3`).
   - Fill: `bg-brand-400` (#F6E3D5 cream) -> `bg-secondary-50` (#FCFCFC near-white) so it
     contrasts against the gold active fill it sits on.
   - Border: keep 1px `accent-500`.
   - Add elevation: `shadow-[0_1px_3px_rgba(0,0,0,0.5)]` (Tailwind arbitrary; there is no
     shared token). This is the single biggest fix for the "flat / stuck-on" look.
   - Hover: border steps to `accent-400` (#E5C158). Use the `hover:` variant inside the
     thumb pseudo-selectors already in the string.

4. Grab area (Baymard - fixes over-sensitivity, currently the input is only 16px tall)
   - The two `<input type="range">` already carry `h-4 w-full` + `inset-0`; bump the row
     and inputs so the transparent hit zone is >=24px:
     - `DualRangeSlider` wrapper `relative h-4` -> `relative h-6`.
     - `THUMB_CLASSES` leading `h-4` -> `h-6`.
     - Move the track div to `top-[11px]` (or `top-2.5`) so it stays centred on the 24px
       row. End labels row unaffected (`gap-2` below stays).
   - Visual thumb + track sizes do NOT grow - only the invisible input height.

5. Focus-visible
   - Reduce offset: `focus-visible:outline-offset-4` -> `focus-visible:outline-offset-2`.
   - Keep `outline-2 outline-accent-500`.

6. End labels ($0 / $1000)
   - Unchanged classes (`type-caption text-text-caption`). Only tighten the gap from the
     track: the `flex flex-col gap-2` wrapper in `DualRangeSlider` -> `gap-1`.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DEFINITION OF DONE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  - Track reads as a 2px hairline in both rest and active colour.
  - Thumbs are near-white 12px discs with a 1px gold ring and a visible soft shadow;
    they lift off both the dark panel and the gold fill.
  - Grab area is >=24px tall (verify: click 10px above/below the visible thumb still
    starts a drag).
  - Keyboard focus shows a tight 2px gold outline.
  - $0 / $1000 labels sit directly under the track.
  - Human eyeballs it on localhost:3000 catalogue filter sidebar (desktop + mobile
    sheet) and signs off.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ZERO SCOPE CREEP - EXPLICITLY OUT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  - No numeric min/max input fields. No histogram / product-count bars. (Baymard
    recommends both - they are separate future issues, NOT this one.)
  - No change to URL contract, debounce, clamp, min<=max, reset, or `history:"replace"`.
  - No new dependency (no Radix/MUI/noUiSlider) - stays native `<input type=range>`.
  - No change to `ResetButton` / `ResetIcon` / `FilterSliderSection` header row.
  - No change to `FilterSidebar.tsx`, tokens, `tailwind.config.ts`, or globals.css.
  - No change to the other filter sliders that import this pattern beyond what falls out
    of the shared `THUMB_CLASSES` / `DualRangeSlider` edits (that shared restyle is
    intended - it is the "single definition of the filter-slider look").
  - Diff should be ~8-12 edited lines in one file.

- When I load a URL with brand, price and sort params set, then I see one chip per active value, with price shown as a single range chip.

- When I click "Clear all" while a search query param is also in the URL, then that query param stays and only the filter/sort params are removed.
- When I press Back right after "Clear all", then all the previous filters and their chips come back in lockstep with the address bar.
- When a param in the URL holds a value with no matching label, then its chip shows the raw value cleanly or is omitted - never a broken or blank chip.
- When price is set to only one bound, then the range chip reads sensibly (e.g. "From $X" or "Up to $Y").
